explain.say: Think of a jigsaw: a piece only clicks in where its bumps and gaps match. DNA works a bit like that. Its ladder rungs are pairs of bases, and they are very fussy about partners. Let's see why.

faq.q: What are the four bases in DNA?
faq.a: Adenine, thymine, cytosine and guanine, written A, T, C and G. The order of these bases along DNA is the genetic code.
asks: Tell me about the four bases

faq.q: Why must a big base pair with a small base?
faq.a: A and G are purines, with two rings; T and C are pyrimidines, with one ring. A purine always pairs with a pyrimidine, so every rung is the same length and the helix stays even.
asks: Tell me about shapes that fit

faq.q: What holds the base pairs together?
faq.a: Hydrogen bonds, which are weak attractions. A and T form two hydrogen bonds, while C and G form three, so C-G pairs hold together slightly more strongly.

faq.q: How does base pairing help DNA copy itself?
faq.a: The two strands unzip, and each one is used as a template. New bases pair up with the old ones, A with T and C with G, making two identical DNA molecules.

faq.q: Who discovered the structure of DNA?
faq.a: James Watson and Francis Crick published the double helix model in 1953, using X-ray images made by Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling, with data also from Maurice Wilkins.

facts: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine using two hydrogen bonds, and cytosine pairs with guanine using three.
The double helix model of DNA was published by Watson and Crick in 1953, based partly on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray work.

quiz.say: One DNA strand reads A T T G C. What does the matching strand read?
quiz.show: One DNA strand reads A T T G C. What does the matching strand read?
quiz.why: A pairs with T and C pairs with G, so ATTGC matches TAACG.

wrong.1: That is the same strand again, not its partner.
wrong.2: This swaps A with G and T with C, which do not pair.

quiz.say: Which base pair is held by three hydrogen bonds?
quiz.show: Which base pair is held by three hydrogen bonds?
quiz.why: Cytosine and guanine form three hydrogen bonds.

wrong.0: A and T form two hydrogen bonds.
wrong.2: A and G are both large bases and do not pair together.
